text.en: Stand in a crowded railway station in any Indian city and look around. India has just 2.4 percent of the world's land, yet about 17.5 percent of the world's people live here, so one out of every six persons on earth is an Indian. In this lesson we learn how many we are, where we live, how fast we grow, why people move, and what happens when cities fill up.

The study of population is one of the most important parts of geography, because the number, composition, distribution and density of people show the workforce of a country.
Population is the total number of people living in a country at a given time, and India is the most populous country in the world.
The census is the whole process of collecting, compiling and analysing demographic, economic and social data about all persons in a country, and it is held once in ten years.
India's first census was taken in 1872, the first complete and synchronous census was in 1881, and the 2011 census was the fifteenth census of India.
Population distribution means the way people are spread over the land, and in India it is very uneven because resources are very unevenly available.
People crowd into industrial centres and good farmland, while high mountains, deserts, thick forests and remote corners are thinly populated or even empty.
Terrain, climate, soil, water, minerals, industries, transport and urbanisation are the major factors that decide where people settle.
Density of population is the number of persons per square kilometre, and in 2011 India's average density was 382 persons per sq km.
Bihar is the most densely populated state and Arunachal Pradesh the least, while among union territories Delhi has 11,297 persons per sq km and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have the lowest density.
Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state with 199.5 million people, followed by Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal and combined Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and these five states hold nearly half of India's people.
Sikkim is the least populous state, and among union territories Delhi tops with 16.75 million people.
Population change means the increase or decrease of population from one period to another, and it depends on the birth rate, the death rate and migration.
Birth rate is the number of live births per thousand people in a year, death rate is the number of deaths per thousand, and the rapid fall in the death rate is the main reason India's population has grown so fast.
Looking at the decadal growth rates, India grew only 5.75 percent in 1911, even fell by 0.31 percent in 1921, then rose steadily to a peak of 24.80 percent in 1971 before slowing down to 17.64 percent in 2011.
Migration is the movement of people across regions and countries, either internal within the country or international between countries.
Internal migration does not change the size of a country's population, but it changes how the people are distributed, and the main stream in India is from villages to cities.
Unemployment and under-employment in villages are push factors, while jobs and higher wages in cities are pull factors.
Population composition means characteristics such as age, sex, literacy and occupation, and studying it shows the social and economic structure of the people.
By age, children under 15 are 29.5 percent and people above 60 are 8 percent, so the dependent population is 37.5 percent and the working-age group of 16 to 59 years is 62.5 percent, which is a huge manpower.
Sex ratio is the number of females per 1,000 males, and India's 2011 ratio is 940, which means fewer women than men.
Kerala has the highest sex ratio of 1,084 and Puducherry 1,038, while Haryana has the lowest among states at 879 and Daman and Diu the lowest among union territories at 618.
Literacy rate is the percentage of people who can read and write, and India's 2011 literacy rate is 74.04 percent, with 82.14 percent for males and 65.46 percent for females, a gap of 16.68 percent.
Kerala has the highest literacy at 93.91 percent and Bihar the lowest among states at 63.82 percent, while Lakshadweep leads the union territories with 92.28 percent.
In the census, those who worked for at least six months or 183 days of the previous year are main workers, those who worked less are marginal workers, and the rest are non-workers.
Too many people put pressure on resources and cause overcrowding, unemployment, a low standard of living, malnutrition, poor use of resources and an unhealthy environment.
Urbanization is the change of a society from rural to urban, and its level is measured by the percentage of people living in towns and cities.
Goa is the most urbanised state and Himachal Pradesh the least, and Tamil Nadu is the second most urbanised major state with 48.4 percent urban people, after Goa and followed by Kerala and Maharashtra.
Rural to urban migration crowds the cities and causes urban sprawl, overcrowding, house shortage, slums, traffic jams, water scarcity, drainage and solid waste problems, and more crime.

problem.en: In 2011 a state has 40 million people in an area of 100,000 sq km. What is its density and is it above India's average of 382?

text.en: Density is population divided by area, so 40,000,000 divided by 100,000 gives 400 persons per sq km.
Compare with the national average of 382.
400 is greater than 382, so this state is more crowded than the country as a whole.

prompt.en: Explain to a classmate why India's population grew so fast after 1921 and why people move from villages to cities.

requiredIdeas.en: Death rate fell rapidly while the birth rate stayed high, so the population grew fast
Migration from rural to urban areas is caused by push factors such as unemployment and pull factors such as jobs and wages
Rural to urban migration changes distribution but not the total size of the country's population

commonMisconceptions.en: Migration within the country increases the total population (it only changes the distribution)
Sex ratio means males per 1000 females (it is females per 1000 males)

points.en: India has 2.4% of the world's land but 17.5% of its people, and the census is held every ten years.
Density 382 per sq km, sex ratio 940, literacy 74.04%, with Kerala leading in sex ratio and literacy.
Growth depends on birth rate, death rate and migration, and the fall in death rate caused rapid growth.
Urbanisation brings slums, traffic and water problems, and Tamil Nadu is the second most urbanised major state.
